meta.title: Finding Gold — Placer gold
meta.author: Ezekiel Minja
meta.description: Finding Gold: a field guide to mineral exploration. Educational — not a design standard.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: Everything so far has been gold locked inside rock. Now the easy kind.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: A lode at surface does not stay there. Rain, frost, roots and acid break the quartz apart, and set the gold free.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: Gold does not weather. It does not rust, it does not dissolve, it does not break down. It simply becomes a loose grain of metal. And that metal is nineteen point three times as dense as water, while the quartz it came out of is two point six five.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: That difference is the whole mechanism. Moving water carries both. The instant it slows, gold drops first.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: So gold gathers exactly where water loses energy. And those places are predictable.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: On the inside of bends, where the flow slackens. Behind boulders, in the eddy downstream. And in bedrock riffles — cracks and ledges across the stream bed that work like a sluice box built by geology.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: Where a tributary joins and the current drops. And where the gradient flattens, as the valley opens out.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: In section, almost all of it sits in the bottom half metre of gravel, resting on bedrock. That layer is the pay streak. It is why placer miners dig to bedrock, and clean the cracks by hand.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: The family. Eluvial, still on the hillside below its lode. Alluvial, in the stream. Beach placers, sorted by waves. And palaeo-placers — ancient river gravels, buried and cemented into rock.

dialogue.speaker: juma
dialogue.text: If placers are the easy gold, why does anyone chase the hard kind?

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: Placers are small, shallow and quickly exhausted. But they need no blasting and very little capital — which is why they are where artisanal and small-scale mining lives, and why it matters to far more people than any big mine does.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: And this. Gold in a stream came from somewhere upstream. Sample up the drainage, watch the grains get coarser and more angular, and they will walk you to the lode.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: A placer is a deposit and a signpost at the same time.
